Description

[edit | edit source]

The ranger is an offensive class that focuses on solid and reliable melee damage while bringing out unique archery based skills with best-in-class utility.

Rangers are a lightly armored offensive class which focuses more on delivering damage than tanking. In terms of combat skills they can use all types of weapons and get dual wield, double attack, triple attack, and kick. They have higher offensive skill caps than any other hybrid class. This, combined with innate attack spells means that rangers will have better and more consistent damage output for comparable equipment. Additionally, rangers are one of only two classes that can do critical blows with archery as a default. All rangers deal double damage with archery to standing targets that are not rooted. Additionally, ranged stance allows for use of archery in short range. Finally, rangers also have fast casting, cooldown controlled nukes that are great for fast-paced play.

In terms of defenses, rangers also get a number of defensive skills including dodge, parry, riposte, block, and disarm. However, they are lower in a number of defensive skill areas. They have a lower skill cap compared to Warriors, and slightly below the Paladin and Shadow Knight class as well. As light tanks with some of the best aggro inducing abilities in the game they can but should not be left to tank for significant periods. They have no skill to reduce the monsters hate for them until the level 50 in the form of the spell Jolt. Indeed, until you have Jolt rangers will need to use snares, roots, or evasive to get out of sticky situations.

Rangers get the highest tracking skill in the game, which helps to find people or enemies within the area. This is particularly useful in the large outdoor zones, and can be used to track corpses of members of your group. Additionally, rangers have a high cap on forage which will all but guarantee you always have food and water to survive on.

In terms of magic Rangers get a range of nice utility spells. They receive both Spirit of Wolf and Force of Nature for run speed and a significant ATK bonus. They also get Harmony of Nature to reduce monster agro ranges and this enables them to single pull out of a group. They have both healing spells and damage shields (the latter of which inflicts unresistable damage). This is coupled with a solid series of HP and AC increasing buffs, as well as some minor stat buffs. Damage wise they receive both direct damage and damage over time spells. They can also snare and root mobs. Despite their magical power they do not have the ability to bind or gate. You can view the full ranger spell list on the chart below.

If you are looking for a class pick with solid and dependable damage output, the best tracking in the game, and a little bit of magic to spice things up this class could be the one for you. You will be able to deal damage, spot heal, and act as a light tank in group content.

Loadout Synergies

[edit | edit source]

Everquest Legends allows for lots of synergies when picking a class loadout. Consider the following choices based on how you want to play the game:

Ranger as Primary Class

[edit | edit source]

Thematically, choosing ranger as your primary class means you are going to be picking a class that has range control. You can fight in close range, you can fight at long range, you can root and/or snare enemies, you can increase your own movement speed; this means that the ranger primaries will always have mobility. To make sure you always have runway, pick extra classes that give you distractions like pets. You will gain more distance control with a pet class like magician, necromancer, or beastlord.

Double down on archery by picking additional ranged combat classes like wizard, druid, magician, necromancer, or enchanter. Your goal is to weave spell and arrow into a pure stream of damage.

To improve melee damage, add berserker, monk, or rogue.

Ranger as Extra Class

[edit | edit source]

Ranger brings unique ranged attack options for any other distance fighter; archery gives you a no-mana alternative to burning your mana bar. This means you have intrinsic synergy with most offensive casters (wizard, necromancer, mage, enchanter, and yes! even druid). Archery is a beautiful filler for any caster that would otherwise be meditating for mana in combat.

Most ranged classes also lack close range escapes and ranger's evasive stance gives you an extra survival tool. Even classes that can FD will appreciate being able to dodge almost all attacks for a few seconds when agro gets pulled.

When using ranger as an extra class you'll find that it shines brightest when fighting mobs with high mitigation thanks to strikethrough and improved attack power. Additionally, rangers have good itemization for melee loadouts and can bring unique items that they otherwise might not have access to like Dark Cloak of the Sky.

Tanks can benefit from adding ranger thanks to gaining access to evasive stance, strikethrough (which prevents riposte) and high-threat generating spells like Snare, as well as AC and damage shield lines.

Religious Considerations

[edit | edit source]

Religion does have a few impacts upon the Ranger class. Rangers that also do fletching (which is *highly* recommended) will want to match their deity choices to the tradeskill source they intend to use; fletchers of Karana will get the ability to craft special bows and Steel Champion arrows from vendors in Surefall Glade, and rangers of Tunare will get the ability to craft special bows and Mithril Champion arrows from vendors in Greater Faydark. If your current unlocked deities does not include Karana or Tunare, consider unlocking one or both in order to use the best arrows that can be fletched.

Note if you choose ranger as an extra class you may be locked out of the absolute best arrows that can be made until you unlock the appropriate deities; thankfully, there are good enough options you will perform well enough.

OUT OF ERA: Historically, Tunare had quested items that appeared as well for rangers once Velious unlocked. This is not a factor you should consider for rangers in Everquest Legends.

Name Description
Balanced Stance All incoming damage is reduced by 10% and your chance to hit is increased by 10%. Endurance regen excluding out of combat bonus regen is doubled. There is no endurance cost to upkeep this stance.
Offensive Stance Outgoing melee damage is increased by 100% and your chance to hit is increased by 25%. Every point of bonus damage dealt consumes an equal amount of endurance, with a reduction based on your strategy skill.

When below 25% endurance, the chance to hit bonus is reduced based on the remaining percent of endurance.

Bonus damage from critical hits and similar effects do not cost endurance.

Evasive Stance You have a 95% chance to evade all incoming attacks. Every point of damage evaded consumes 2 endurance, with a reduction based on your strategy skill. Evasion will fail if you have insufficient endurance, or while playing dead.
Ranged Stance Your range attack has no minimum distance, gains a 25% accuracy bonus, and can double and triple attack. Every point of damage consumes endurance, with a reduction based on your strategy skill.
Recovery Invocation You regenerate mana twice as fast and spells have a 5% reduced mana cost.

Out of combat regen bonus is not affected. While out of combat, the regeneration modifier of this invocation is active even if this invocation is not.

Inversion Invocation Shifts two-thirds of spell cast time into the global recovery time and 20% of the mana cost into half as much in endurance cost.
Over Channel Invocation Cast spells have a -150 resist adjust plus another -15 for every non-hybrid caster class at a cost of 10% of the mana cost in endurance.
Spellblade Invocation Treats the first spell-gem slot as a proc that consumes both mana and endurance on activation.

40% of the spells mana cost is paid as mana and 20% as endurance. The spell must have a reuse time less than or equal to its cast time.

Divine Invocation Spending mana will heal the group member with the lowest hp percentage by that amount.

For every additional wisdom class, this will repeat with a heal for 33% of the mana spent.

FAQ

[edit | edit source]

Q: What stances does a ranger get?

A: Rangers get balanced stance, offensive stance, evasive stance, and ranged stance.

Q: What invocations does a ranger get?

A: Rangers get divine, inversion, recovery, overchannel, and spellblade invocations.

Q: Does a ranger ever get to critical hit? I am able to critical with the bow occasionally, but never with my 1hs/2hs.

A: Yes, it may not be available at level 1, but certainly by level 10 rangers can get melee critical hits without any AAs.

Q: What level do you suggest doing the ivy etched armor quest? And how difficult is it?

A: There are different Ivy Etched armor quests, each with different level NPC's you have to fight in order to obtain the items needed. The easiest and lowest level Ivy quest being the bracers, (which you can be complete easily in your 20's in a group), and hardest being the tunic/leggings, (which can be done solo in your 40's).


Q: Do Rangers get the ability to summon animals?

A: Unless you have an item that has the effect of summoning an animal, nope.


Q: What does increasing your level in tracking do?

A: It increases the range of your tracking, allowing you to find farther away mobs and improving visibility on your minimap.

Q: How do I make the best of archery?

A: Ranger archery in Everquest Legends is best utilized through the ranged stance. It removes the minimum range restriction on your bow and allows you to double and triple shot with bows while in the stance. This means you can function somewhat in melee while using the bow, but more importantly gives you great synergy with caster classes by giving you a damage method not reliant on mana.

Q: Do rangers ever learn to track their corpse or the corpse of other player characters?

A: You can track other character corpses only if they are in your group, and they have died while your in the same zone. Their corpse will stay on your tracking until they zone back in.

Q: What cities are the ranger guilds located? Are the guilds the only place a ranger can go to practice and buy spells?

A: Surefall Glade, Neriak, Rivervale, New Sebilis Expedition, and Kelethin are the current cities (July 2026) a ranger can practice with a guild trainer. There are also spell vendors in those zones. A single trainer named Morin Shadowbane is also available in Kithicor Woods, but no spell vendors. A large portion of ranger spells are also druid spells, which are available throughout Norrath at druid guilds and rings.

Q: How does a ranger make arrows and at what level are they effective?

A: You first need a fletching kit, a point, shaft, nock, and fletching skill. Put one of each component into the fletching kit, hit combine and hope that it works. You can merge your arrows up until they reach +10 like any other item. Keep in mind that crafted items are harder to get higher copies of, and thus you may need to plan on making 1024 arrows just to reach +10 of your desired arrow. Check out Fletching for more information.

Q: Would a Ranger get less experience if they are in Wolf Form?

A: Nope, experience stays the same.
